title: Monetary Policy Report—January 2026
summary: The Bank of Canada held its target overnight rate at 2.25% (Bank Rate 2.5%, deposit rate 2.20%) amid elevated US tariff disruption and trade uncertainty. The Canadian economy is expected to grow at approximately 1.25% over the projection horizon while CPI inflation remains near the 2% target, with excess supply roughly offsetting upward cost pressures. The outlook is characterized by unusually high risks due to geopolitical uncertainty and the ongoing review of the Canada-United States-Mexico Agreement.
key_points: Bank of Canada maintained target overnight rate at 2.25%, with Bank Rate at 2.5% and deposit rate at 2.20%
CPI inflation remains near the 2% target, with excess supply offsetting upward cost pressures
Economic growth projected at approximately 1.25% over the projection horizon, subdued by US tariffs and slowing population growth
Canadian businesses are adapting by expanding exports to non-US countries and reducing reliance on US imports
The Canada-United States-Mexico Agreement is under review, with outcomes and economic impacts remaining highly uncertain
Global growth expected to remain solid, supported by AI investment boom and fiscal stimulus in major economies
why_it_matters: This quarterly monetary policy report provides the official economic outlook from the Bank of Canada. The decision to hold rates at 2.25% signals a policy holding pattern while the Bank monitors tariff impacts and inflation trajectory. Market participants tracking CAD, Canadian equities, and bonds should note that the Bank sees balanced risks between excess supply and cost pressures from tariffs, keeping inflation near target despite trade disruptions.
macro_context: The report identifies US tariffs as the primary disruptive force for the Canadian economy, with structural adjustments expected to take time. The Bank projects modest growth (~1.25%) while maintaining inflation near the 2% target, suggesting neither urgent tightening nor easing is warranted. Risks are described as 'unusually high' due to trade agreement uncertainty and geopolitical factors. Global conditions are more supportive, driven by AI-related investment and fiscal stimulus elsewhere.
